formats.key: Mint1155(uint256 tokenId,uint256 supply,string tokenURI,Part[] creators,Part[] royalties)Part(address account,uint96 value)
effects: The signature lets creators[0] (the minter, whose address is the top 160 bits of tokenId), or any operator the minter has approved, including Rarible's default-approved transfer proxies, create token `tokenId` on this collection with a total supply of `supply`.
The caller picks who receives the minted copies and how many (up to `supply`). The recipient is not in the signed message.
The first mint permanently records the creators list and their shares (which must sum to 10000), the royalty receivers and rates paid on secondary sales, and the token URI.
The signature has no nonce and no expiry. It stays valid until the token is first minted. After that, later mints skip signature checks until the supply is used up.
Nothing leaves the signer's wallet. No approval is granted over the signer's existing tokens, and no native value is involved.
formats.shown: The intent "Lazy Mint ERC-1155" sits above raw fields: the token ID, the URI, the supply, and the creator and royalty addresses and shares as raw numbers in basis points.

findings.title: Mint1155 has no interpolatedIntent, so the sentence never gives the supply or the royalty terms being fixed.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json format Mint1155: "intent": "Lazy Mint ERC-1155", no interpolatedIntent. ERC1155Lazy.mintAndTransfer: _saveSupply(data.tokenId, data.supply); _saveRoyalties(data.tokenId, data.royalties).
findings.fix: Add an interpolatedIntent such as "Authorize lazy mint of {supply} copies of token {tokenId}", and use the intent "Authorize lazy mint of an ERC-1155 token".

findings.title: Mint1155 shows creator and royalty accounts and shares as separate parallel arrays the signer cannot easily pair.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json fields: "creators.[].account", "creators.[].value", "royalties.[].account", "royalties.[].value" are four separate fields. ERC1155Lazy._saveCreators pushes each (account, value) pair together.
findings.fix: Use a nested field on "creators.[]" and on "royalties.[]" whose sub-fields are account and value, so each address is shown with its share.

findings.title: Mint1155 shows royalty and creator addresses as raw hex and shares as raw basis points.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json: "royalties.[].account" format "raw", "royalties.[].value" format "raw" with the label "Royalties value (10000 = 100%)"; the creators fields are the same.
findings.fix: Use addressName (types eoa/contract, source local/ens) for the accounts, and the unit format with decimals 2 and base "%" for the shares.

findings.title: Mint1155 does not show the recipient of the minted tokens, because the signed message does not carry it.
findings.evidence: ERC1155Lazy.mintAndTransfer(data, address to, uint256 _amount): `to` and `_amount` come from the caller, and the Mint1155 typehash has no recipient.
findings.fix: No descriptor change can show it. A label or the intent could say the minter chooses the recipient.

findings.title: Mint1155 does not say the signature never expires and can be used by default-approved Rarible proxies.
findings.evidence: ERC1155Lazy.mintAndTransfer: require(minter == sender || isApprovedForAll(minter, sender)). ERC1155DefaultApproval.isApprovedForAll returns true for defaultApprovals[_operator]. The typehash has no nonce or deadline.
findings.fix: No field exists to show it. The intent wording could mention that the signature lets Rarible mint on your behalf.

findings.title: Mint1155 tokenId packs the minter address in its top 160 bits, shown only as a raw integer.
findings.evidence: ERC1155Lazy.mintAndTransfer: address minter = address(data.tokenId >> 96); require(minter == data.creators[0].account).
findings.fix: No format extracts the high bits of a uint256. The descriptor could note in the label that the token ID encodes the first creator.
